question.text: Which of the following BEST describes the difference between Strategic Asset Allocation (SAA) and Tactical Asset Allocation (TAA)?

answer.text: SAA is based on short-term market outlook while TAA sets the long-term policy mix
SAA requires daily rebalancing while TAA is reviewed only annually
SAA and TAA are identical concepts; the terms are used interchangeably in portfolio management
SAA sets the long-term target allocation based on investor objectives, while TAA involves short-term deviations from SAA to exploit perceived market opportunities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-A pages 263-264, SAA is the long-term target policy allocation derived from the investor's characteristics and objectives. TAA is a short-term decision taken within the SAA framework to exploit market opportunities. Page 264 notes that asset allocation policy explains about 40 percent of return variability across portfolios and about 90 percent of return variability for a single fund over time. The Trap: The first option reverses the definitions — a classic exam trick. The second option fabricates rebalancing frequency requirements. SAA and TAA are distinct concepts, never interchangeable. Note: Read the workbook's "40 percent across portfolios / 90 percent single-fund-over-time" distinction carefully — these are two different measurements of allocation's influence on returns.
